question: What walking speed is generally used to calculate pedestrian clearance time, and what alternative speed may be used with an extended push-button feature?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The pedestrian clearance time is generally calculated using a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second, measured from the curb or edge of pavement to the far side of the traveled way or a suitable median. Where an extended push-button press feature is installed to give slower pedestrians a longer clearance time, a walking speed of up to 4 feet per second may be used to evaluate the sufficiency of the clearance time. A slower speed (less than 3.5 ft/s) should be considered where slower pedestrians or wheelchair users routinely use the crosswalk. Guidance (recommended): - "Except as provided in Paragraph 8 of this Section, the pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient to allow a pedestrian crossing in the crosswalk who left the curb or edge of pavement at the end of the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication to travel at a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second to at least the far side of the traveled way or to a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait." - "Where pedestrians who walk slower than 3.5 feet per second, or pedestrians who use wheelchairs, routinely use the crosswalk, a walking speed of less than 3.5 feet per second should be considered in determining the pedestrian clearance time." - The total of the walk interval and pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient for a pedestrian leaving the pedestrian detector (or a point 6 feet behind the curb face or pavement edge) at the beginning of the WALK indication to cross at 3 feet per second; any additional time needed should be added to the walk interval. Options (permitted): - "A walking speed of up to 4 feet per second may be used to evaluate the sufficiency of the pedestrian clearance time at locations where an extended push button press function has been installed to provide slower pedestrians an opportunity to request and receive a longer pedestrian clearance time." Passive pedestrian detection may also be used to automatically adjust the clearance time based on the pedestrian's actual walking speed or actual clearance of the crosswalk. - The additional time provided by an extended push button press may be added to either the walk interval or the pedestrian change interval. - Pedestrians may be provided with additional features such as increased crossing time, audible beaconing, or a speech push button information message as a result of an extended push button press. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 4I-4 illustrates the pedestrian intervals, showing that the calculated pedestrian clearance time (see Section 4I.07) spans the pedestrian change interval and buffer interval. [Image 3] Figure 2B-27 shows the R10-32P plaque ("PUSH BUTTON FOR 2 SECONDS FOR EXTRA CROSSING TIME") associated with the extended push-button press feature. [Image 5] Page 765 contains the Section 4I.06 text stating the 3.5 ft/s recommended speed and the optional 4 ft/s speed with an extended push button press. Citations: - Section 4I.06 Guidance §7 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Option §8 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Option §9 (p.725) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §10 (p.725) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §14 (p.725) - Section 4K.05 Option §1 (p.734) - Figure 4I-4 (p.724) - Figure 2B-27 (p.130) - Page 765
gold_answer: The general walking speed is 3.5 feet per second. Up to 4 feet per second may be used to evaluate sufficiency where an extended push-button press provides slower pedestrians a longer clearance time.
